character_sheet: The Kraken is a flying squid the size of a tower: a mantle head with two eyes, a siphon jet and an eight-flap mouth ringed by 41 teeth, a front, centre and back body, a three-piece tail with two fins, four eight-segment tentacles dangling below and two eight-segment arm tentacles ending in suckers (ModelKraken.createBodyLayer, ModelKraken.java:249-594). It has 1000 HP and 40 attack (MobStats.KRAKEN, createAttributes Kraken.java:107-115), a blue boss bar (:57-58), fears no fire (:131-133) and never touches the ground: it steers itself between flight targets it re-picks on arrival or a 1-in-250 roll (customServerAiStep :261-290, pickNewFlightTarget :292-358, applyFlightMovement :453-460), brings rain and thunder wherever it goes (:204-220) and drops a lightning bolt sixteen blocks below itself on a 1-in-400 roll (:251-259). On a 1-in-8 tick it looks for the nearest survival player in sight, or half the time for any living prey — ground-bound things and unridden mounts (:663-685) — flies to fifteen blocks above them and, when the point fifteen below itself is within reach, GRABS them (searchForPrey :371-396, attackWithSomething :541-552): the victim is carried fifteen blocks beneath it toward y 200, squeezed on a 1-in-50 roll and let go above y 190, on a 1-in-250 roll or when the Kraken is hurt (handleCaughtEntity :398-444, hurt :562-586). Hurt by a player above quarter health it turns on them (:565-570); below a quarter it climbs, and at an eighth of its health above y 130 it calls ten more Krakens (:332-357). It leaves the world above y 256 or after 3600 ticks (:287-289, :136-145), and spawns above y 50 under a clear column (checkSpawnRules :718-723). Read it as a slow airborne squid: tentacles trailing in long waves, the two arms snapping down for the grab.
size_notes: Drawn at x1.0 of the rig, a third of that while PlayNicely (KrakenRenderer.java:28, applied :37-45; shadow 1.0) on a 512x512 sheet (ModelKraken.java:594); 4 x 15 block hitbox (ModEntities.java:199-200; 1.33 x 5 while PlayNicely, Kraken.getDefaultDimensions :176-180). The tentacles are eight-segment chains the code positions segment by segment, 30 units apart — key the joints, never the positions.

groups.name: fin_right
groups.amplitude: pi x 0.15 = 0.471 rad (27 deg) about zero
groups.plain: the right tail fin rolls on its own slow rhythm
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 0.43: the natural period is 14.6 ticks

groups.name: fin_left
groups.amplitude: pi x 0.14 = 0.44 rad (25 deg) about zero
groups.plain: the left tail fin rolls on a slower rhythm than the right, so the two never quite agree
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 0.32: the natural period is 19.6 ticks

groups.name: tentacles
groups.axis: x and y (a pitch wave and a yaw wave at slightly different rates)
groups.amplitude: pi x 0.1 = 0.314 rad (18 deg) on every segment, each 0.314 rad (18 deg of phase) behind the one before, about a splay on the root and half of it on the second segment (tentacle 1: yaw +0.44; 2 and 3: pitch +0.26; 4: yaw −0.44); the pitch wave at 0.101 / 0.097 / 0.093 / 0.087 rad/tick and the yaw wave at 0.102 / 0.098 / 0.092 / 0.088 for tentacles 1-4 (the pitch sign −1); each segment placed 30 units along the one before; never changed by the attacking flag
groups.plain: the four lower tentacles trail in slow travelling waves, each tentacle at its own slightly different pair of rates so they drift apart, whatever the Kraken is doing
groups.math: for tentacle d (1..4), segment k (0..7): p_k.xRot = xoff_k - cos(t * differ_d - k * 0.314) * pi * 0.1; p_k.yRot = yoff_k - cos(t * ydiffer_d - k * 0.314) * pi * 0.1 (xoff / yoff on k = 0, halved on k = 1, zero after); positions along the chain by sin/cos x 30
groups.omega_note: the classic phases are ageInTicks x 0.101 / 0.097 / 0.093 / 0.087 (pitch) and x 0.102 / 0.098 / 0.092 / 0.088 (yaw): periods from 62 to 72 ticks; the seed's 0.1 stands for the family

groups.name: arms
groups.amplitude: calm: pi x 0.1 = 0.314 rad (18 deg) on every segment at 0.2 rad/tick (the yaw wave at 0.1), each 18 degrees of phase behind the one before, about a −0.25 pitch on the root (half on the second segment), the left arm's pitch wave negative and the right's positive; attacking: pi x 0.03 = 0.094 rad (5.4 deg) at 0.5 rad/tick with no splay — the arms straighten and quiver; the suckers ride the tips 30 units on
groups.plain: the two arm tentacles wave like the others at rest and straighten into a fast fine quiver while the attacking flag is set — the grab's pose
groups.math: att = attacking; differ = att ? 0.5 : 0.2; amp = att ? 0.03 : 0.1; xoff = att ? 0 : -0.25; s = -1 (left, tentacle 5) / +1 (right, tentacle 6); p_k.xRot = xoff_k + s * cos(t * differ - k * 0.314) * pi * amp; p_k.yRot = -cos(t * 0.1 - k * 0.314) * pi * amp; Sucktioncup = the tip's angles, placed 30 units on
groups.phase: the synced DATA_ATTACKING byte (Kraken.java:44; set at :550 on the grab, cleared at :450 on release) selects
groups.omega_note: the classic phase calm is ageInTicks x 0.2 (period 31.4 ticks; the yaw wave x 0.1, 62.8 ticks); attacking x 0.5 (period 12.6 ticks)

groups.name: mouth
groups.amplitude: when the latch picks it: pi x 0.015 = 0.047 rad (2.7 deg) on the eight mouth flaps about ±0.38, and seven times that (19 deg) on the 41 teeth about their rests (each tooth's own sign); otherwise still
groups.plain: the mouth flaps and teeth twitch in the periods a per-entity random latch picks for them — a few periods in ten at rest, half of them while attacking — and hold still otherwise
groups.math: at each rising zero-crossing of cos(t * 0.66): ri1 = attacking ? nextInt(4) : nextInt(10); m = (ri1 == 1 || ri1 == 3) ? cos(t * 0.5) * pi * 0.015 : 0; MouthN.xRot / yRot = ±0.38 ± m; ToothN.xRot / yRot = rest ± 7m
groups.phase: a per-entity random latch (RenderInfo ri1, re-rolled at each rising zero-crossing of a 0.66 rad/tick wave, :622-635); the attacking flag loads the dice
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 0.5: the natural period is 12.6 ticks; the latch re-rolls every 9.5 ticks

behaviour: The two tail fins roll on their own rhythms — the right 27 degrees at 0.43 rad/tick, the left 25 degrees at 0.32 — so they never agree (ModelKraken.java:599-600). The head, eyes, jet, the three body blocks and the tail itself are static; nothing reads the walking speed, the walk position or the look angles.

The four lower tentacles trail in slow travelling waves, 18 degrees on every segment and 18 degrees of phase between segments, each tentacle at its own pair of rates (a pitch wave at 0.087-0.101 rad/tick and a yaw wave at 0.088-0.102), the root splayed and the chain placed 30 units segment by segment (:716-719, dangleTentacle :842-921); the attacking flag never touches them.

The two arm tentacles wave the same way at rest (0.2 rad/tick, splayed −0.25 at the root) and, while the synced DATA_ATTACKING byte is set (Kraken.java:44, raised on the grab at :550, cleared on release at :450), straighten and quiver 5 degrees at 0.5 rad/tick — the pose of the hold; the suckers ride the tips (:604-617).

The mouth flaps twitch 2.7 degrees and the 41 teeth 19 degrees at 0.5 rad/tick only in the periods a per-entity random latch picks — 2 in 10 at rest, 2 in 4 attacking, re-rolled every 9.5 ticks (:622-714).

The grab (attackWithSomething, Kraken.java:541-552), the squeeze on the held victim (:435-437), the reinforcements (:339-357) and the lightning (:251-259) are rolled by the AI — nothing in the code fires an animation for them.

locked_bones_note: The design's section 6 ModelKraken row (geckolib_migration_design.md:450): 'Head [5,4] @1; Centerbody/Frontbody/Backbody [6,5] @0.5; eight structural tentacle roots (Tent11, Tent21, …) [1.4,4] @0.25; Tailbase1/Tailtip [2,3] @0.25; fins [2,1] @0.25'. Head, Centerbody, Frontbody, Backbody, Tailbase1 and Tailtip resolve as written. 'eight structural tentacle roots' does not resolve as counted: the port model has SIX tentacle chains (Tent1x to Tent6x, eight segments each — ModelKraken.createBodyLayer; four dangling, two arms), so the six roots Tent11, Tent21, Tent31, Tent41, Tent51 and Tent61 are listed and the owner reconciles the count. 'fins' taken as Finleft / Finright. The row asks that the part count and packets be benchmarked before every tentacle root is accepted.
formulas: `ModelKraken.poseFrom` and `dangleTentacle` (ModelKraken.java:606-728 and :850-929; orig ModelKraken.java:1030-1249 in `render` (func_78088_a, :1023-1251; func_78087_a at :1259-1261 is a bare super call) with `dangle_tentacle` :1263-1372, wingspeed 1.0 from `new ModelKraken(1.0f)` in orig ClientProxyOreSpawn.java:444 - the port's ANIM_SPEED): the right fin rolls by the cosine of the age in ticks times 0.43, times pi, times 0.15, the left fin by the cosine of the age times 0.32, times pi, times 0.14. Each of the six tentacles is eight rings: the root ring pitches by its pitch offset plus its sign times the cosine of the age times its pitch rate, times pi, times its amplitude, and yaws by its yaw offset minus the cosine of the age times its yaw rate, times pi, times the amplitude; each following ring lags a further 0.314159 radians, halves the offsets on the second ring and drops them from the third, and is placed 30 units from the ring before it - down by the sine of that ring's pitch times the cosine of its yaw, back by the cosine of its pitch times the cosine of its yaw, across by the sine of its yaw times the cosine of its pitch. The rates are 0.101 / 0.102 (the first tentacle), 0.097 / 0.098 (the second), 0.093 / 0.092 (the third), 0.087 / 0.088 (the fourth) and 0.2 / 0.1 for the two front tentacles; the offsets 0.26 of pitch on the second and third, 0.44 and -0.44 of yaw on the first and fourth, -0.25 of pitch on the front pair; the sign -1 on every tentacle but the sixth; the amplitude 0.1. Attacking, the front pair stiffens: rate 0.5, amplitude 0.03, no pitch offset. The two suction cups ride 30 units past the eighth ring of the front tentacles and copy its pitch and yaw. The mouth twitch is latched per entity: when the cosine of the age times 0.66, times pi, times 0.15 is negative but its value 0.1 tick ahead positive, the latch's two integers are re-rolled from the entity's random - 0 to 9 and 0 to 14 at rest, 0 to 3 and 0 to 2 attacking - and while the first is 1 or 3 the eight mouth parts pitch or yaw by their 0.38 rests plus or minus the cosine of the age times 0.5, times pi, times 0.015 (else the rests alone), and the forty-one teeth by their 0.3 .. 0.39 rests plus or minus seven times that. The walk, the walking speed and the head angles play no part; the classic renderer draws the whole model turned 90 degrees about X (ModelKraken.renderToBuffer :733, orig :1137), which the descriptor's constant render transform carries. The GeckoLib hook is the same (KrakenGeoReplacement.applyCustomAnimations).
